requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec exactly: entities with slug unique 'entities_slug_unique' + softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:16-22); entity_memberships with cascading FKs, role default 'employee', stored generated owner_seq "case when role = 'owner' then 1 else null end" and unique indexes 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' / 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (create_entity_memberships_table.php:17-28). Contract met: Entity::getRouteKeyName/memberships/users/owner() (app/Models/Entity.php:22-57), EntityMembership role cast + owner/admin/employee scopes + relations (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:23-74), UserRole::manageable() (app/Models/UserRole.php:16-19), User::memberships/entities/membershipFor (app/Models/User.php:27-50), factories with states, both policies with the required bool methods. Policy logic matches the rules; docs/database-schema.md updated to drop owner_membership_id.

conventions.evidence: Authorization lives in app/Policies; #[Fillable] attribute matches the existing User model style (app/Models/Entity.php:14, EntityMembership.php:12); migrations have reversible down() with generator-style timestamped names; PHPDoc on public methods; docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] updated in the same change. No Actions needed since there are no domain writes in scope.

security.evidence: Mass assignment restricted via #[Fillable]; policies default-deny non-members via membershipFor(...)?->role with strict in_array (EntityPolicy.php:46-53, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:37-40); owner membership protected from delete and role reassignment (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:17-27); DB-level one-owner invariant. No input handling or output in this change.

tests.evidence: Pest tests cover schema (index names, duplicate slug/membership/owner rejection, owner_seq values, role DB default, cascades: EntitySchemaTest.php), model/factory/contract (EntityModelTest.php), and every policy ability for owner/admin/employee/stranger/other-entity admin including denial paths (EntityPolicyTest.php, EntityMembershipPolicyTest.php). Minor gap: no test goes through Gate/can() to confirm policy discovery, and manageSettings is not checked for otherEntityAdmin.

simplicity.evidence: owner() reuses the scope: 'return $this->memberships()->owner();' (Entity.php:55); policies share small private helpers roleIn/isOwnerOrAdmin; no extra layers or abstractions. Small duplication of isOwnerOrAdmin across the two policies is acceptable.

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods; explanatory comment on why NULLs don't collide in the unique index (create_entity_memberships_table.php:19-20); docblocks state each rule; tests named after the business rule they check. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Everything serves the task; no routes, session, pages or translations. Small extra: docs/database-schema.md removes the proposed 'string locale_default' column from the entities diagram (lines 544-545 of the diff), which is not part of replacing owner_membership_id.

issues.explanation: assignRole denies any change to the owner's membership, a restriction not stated in the task; it is a sensible guard for the one-owner invariant but should be confirmed or recorded in business-rules.md.
The proposed 'locale_default' column is removed from the entities diagram, which goes beyond replacing owner_membership_id and silently drops a planned field.
Policies are only tested by calling them directly; one Gate/can() test would confirm they are auto-discovered, and manageSettings is not checked for an admin of another entity.
isOwnerOrAdmin is duplicated in both policies; it could live on User or EntityMembership, but at this size that's acceptable.

review.summary: The change adds the entities/entity_memberships migrations, including the portable one-owner generated column and unique index, plus the Entity, EntityMembership and UserRole models, factories and both policies, with thorough Pest tests and updated schema docs and CHANGELOG. It meets the contract and the conventions closely. The only points are an extra assignRole restriction on the owner membership that the task does not mention and a small unrelated doc edit, so it is approve-with-nits.
